# UIAO — Reference Engine for the Federal Organization Compliance Series {.unnumbered}

The [Federal Organization Compliance Series](../federal-aan-series/index.qmd) is
deliberately **engine-neutral**: wherever a book needs evidence or authorization
tooling, it speaks to the open
[Evidence & Authorization Contract](../federal-aan-series/AAN_Evidence_Contract_Spec.qmd)
— compliance spine in, OSCAL AP/AR/POA&M out — and names no engine. Any
conformant evidence engine may implement it.

**This volume is the engine side of that arrow.** It documents how UIAO — one
conformant implementation — satisfies the contract: which controls it keeps
closed and how, where it actively participates in the architecture, how its rule
set reconciles against the FedRAMP CR26 indicator catalog (including the honest
gaps), and the decision framework for adopting it — or any other engine — as the
series' evidence layer.

The dependency is one-way by doctrine: **this volume names and consumes the
series; the series never names this engine.** If a different engine is selected,
every book here is replaced by that engine's equivalents and the series is
untouched — which is the point of the contract.

The series states its side of that arrow in its own
[Vol X — Governance-Substrate Integration](../federal-aan-series/Vol_X_Book_00_FedAAN_Governance_Substrate_Integration_Overview.qmd)
overview: how the series' evidence binds to a governance substrate through the
[Evidence & Authorization Contract](../federal-aan-series/AAN_Evidence_Contract_Spec.qmd),
in the series' engine-neutral voice. This volume is the engine-side counterpart
to that overview — the same arrow, named from the engine end.

## The books

| Book | What it answers |
|---|---|
| [01 — Control Continuation & Closure](01-control-continuation-and-closure.qmd) | Per control surface: the series closes it once by architecture — how does the engine keep it closed continuously? |
| [02 — Active-Participant Map](02-active-participant-map.qmd) | Where the engine is an active participant in the architecture, not just an observer |
| [03 — ADR-111 ↔ CR26 KSI Reconciliation](03-adr111-cr26-ksi-reconciliation.qmd) | How the internal rule set maps to the official FedRAMP CR26 indicator catalog |
| [04 — Decision-Gate Memo](04-decision-gate-memo.qmd) | Is this the correct engine? The five adoption gates, the risks, and the conditional-adopt recommendation |
| [05 — ConMon Continuation Map](05-conmon-continuation-map.qmd) | The engine-side companion to Vol IV Book 06 (Authorization Package & ConMon) |
| [06 — Federal ConMon Reporting Reference](06-federal-conmon-reporting-reference.qmd) | The federal continuous-monitoring reporting requirements the engine must serve |
| [07 — Reporting-Egress Actuator](07-reporting-egress-actuator.qmd) | Feature documentation: dry-run-safe reporting egress at the governed actuation ceiling |
| [08 — CR26 Reconciliation Findings](08-cr26-reconciliation-findings.qmd) | The executed reconciliation and its spine write-back |

::: {.callout-note}
## Count honesty
These books carry the engine's real coverage numbers — including the
zero-coverage KSI themes and dated gaps — per the series' count-honesty
discipline. "N/N satisfied" claims are internal-decomposition claims until the
CR26 reconciliation in Books 03/08 is reflected externally.
:::
